description: End-to-end verification of the real client/server flow and documentation of how to run and test everything. Depends on FEAT-001..003. Proves the definition of done: a genuine cross-session flow works against the server (not localStorage), with documented commands. Also documents deployment posture (frontend stays on S3+CloudFront; backend + managed Postgres as a separate service) without inventing an undecided AWS compute service or applying Terraform (CLI not installed).
steps: Provide a single documented local dev sequence: start Postgres (server/scripts/db.sh), run backend migrations + `npm run dev` in server/, and `npm run dev` for the frontend with VITE_API_BASE pointed at the backend. Confirm the frontend loads against the live server.

Run an end-to-end check of the real flow against the server (two browser sessions/tabs OR an automated HTTP+WS script driving two sessions): create user A and user B, A adds B by friend code, open a direct chat, A sends a message and B receives it via WebSocket with correct read-state (B's unread increments, clears on markRead, A sees 'read' after B reads), A sends a gift to B, B accepts (bubble flips to '사용중 · N일 남음' and ownership transfers), and run at least one further lifecycle action (e.g. use or extend, plus a rejected/authorization-failure case). Capture the exact commands/steps used and the observed results. If done via a script, place it under server/ or a scripts/ dir and document it.

Update README.md (or add server/README.md) with: backend architecture summary (Fastify + Postgres + REST + WS, session-cookie auth, domain-code reuse, single-instance in-process WS fan-out, no Redis yet), the exact run commands (Postgres via docker run, backend, frontend, env vars), the test commands (frontend `npm test`; backend `npm test` with Postgres running), and the idempotency/authorization guarantees. Keep the existing localStorage demo-mode explanation but note the server-backed mode.

Document deployment posture without fabricating: frontend continues on private S3 + CloudFront (existing infra-tf); the backend deploys as a separate service with separately provisioned managed PostgreSQL, isolated dev/prod, managed secrets, DB backups, logs, monitoring, health checks (GET /health exists). Explicitly note the concrete AWS backend compute service is not yet decided and that backend IaC is deferred (Terraform CLI not installed in this environment). Do NOT invent a specific compute service or write speculative backend Terraform.

Final green pass: root `npm test && npm run build && npm run typecheck`; server `npm test && npm run typecheck && npm run build` with Postgres up. Confirm `git status` shows all intended changes staged/committed on the feature branch and that .kiro/ remains uncommitted.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, reproducible local setup brings up Postgres + backend + frontend and the frontend operates against the live server.

The full real flow (create users, add friend, direct chat, message with read state, gift send + accept + one more lifecycle action + an authorization-rejection case) is verified against the server and the commands/results are recorded.

README (root and/or server) documents run commands, test commands, env vars, and the architecture/guarantees; deployment posture is documented as deferred for backend compute without inventing a service.
Both frontend and backend test/build/typecheck pass in a final combined run; .kiro/ is not committed.
verification: Root: `npm test && npm run build && npm run typecheck`.
Server (Postgres running): `npm test && npm run typecheck && npm run build`.
Execute the documented e2e sequence/script and confirm messages, read state, and gift lifecycle propagate via the server + WebSocket across two sessions.
`git status` confirms feature branch has the changes committed and .kiro/ is untracked.
findings:
COMPLETED on branch feat/backend (committed alongside e2e + docs). The full cross-session flow is PROVEN against the REAL server + REAL PostgreSQL 15 + REAL WebSocket (not localStorage, not mocks).

E2E SCRIPT (server/scripts/e2e.ts, run via `npm run e2e` in server/): boots the DB as a child process over a unix socket (same native-child harness as the vitest globalSetup — required because each execute_bash runs in an ephemeral bubblewrap PID+network namespace where cross-command loopback is EHOSTUNREACH and backgrounded servers are reaped), builds the Fastify app in-process, listens on a real ephemeral port, opens TWO real ws WebSocket clients (A and B) plus two cookie jars, drives the whole flow via real HTTP fetch + WS, asserts, and exits nonzero on failure. Last run: 52 assertions passed, exit 0.

WHAT THE E2E PROVES (all against the live server): (1) create user A (홍길동) + B (김철수) with server-issued friend codes, distinct sessions/cookies; unauthenticated WS closed 1008. (2) A adds B by friend code -> A→B friendship exists, reverse B→A does NOT (directional), duplicate rejected with '이미 친구' reason, A receives WS 'friends' change. (3) openDirectChat idempotent: 2nd open from A and open from B both return the SAME chatId, exactly 1 direct room. (4) A sends message -> B receives WS 'messages' push; B unread=1, A's own=0; markRead clears B unread to 0 and advances B's lastReadAt as seen by A ('read'); no-op markRead emits nothing; retry with same clientKey does not duplicate. (5) gift: A sends gift to B -> gift order + gift message land atomically in the same chat, B gets WS 'gifts' push; ACCEPT by outsider C rejected ('당사자'), ACCEPT by wrong actor A rejected ('받는 사람'), state stays 'paid'; FORCE_EXPIRE rejected 400; B ACCEPT -> status accepted + 90-day voucher + ownership stays receiver B; EXTEND once -> ~180 days, 2nd EXTEND rejected (1-time limit); duplicate gift clientKey -> still 1 order.

DOCS: root README.md gained a '서버 모드' section (local dev sequence with VITE_API_BASE + PORT/DATABASE_URL/COOKIE_SECRET/DEV_TOOLS env table, backend architecture summary: Fastify+PG+REST+WS, HttpOnly signed session-cookie as sole actor identity, domain-code reuse, single-instance in-process WS fan-out with NO Redis yet / Redis Pub/Sub as future path, idempotency + server-side authorization + FORCE_EXPIRE blocked + no prod reset + GET /health), updated the '두 사람이 대화' section to demo-mode, updated limitations to distinguish demo vs server mode, updated the test section (frontend 77, backend 41 self-contained DB, e2e command with the 52-assertion flow described + sandbox one-process rationale), and added a 'backend deployment (planned, not applied)' subsection: frontend stays on private S3+CloudFront; backend as a separate service with separately provisioned managed PostgreSQL, isolated dev/prod, managed secrets, DB backups, logs/monitoring, health checks; concrete AWS compute service explicitly NOT decided and backend IaC DEFERRED (Terraform CLI not installed) — no invented compute service, no speculative backend Terraform. server/README.md gained the e2e section + updated verification list.

FINAL GREEN PASS: root `npm test` = 77 passed, `npm run build` ok, `npm run typecheck` ok. server `npm test` = 41 passed (self-contained native Postgres child), `npm run typecheck` ok, `npm run build` ok. `npm run e2e` exit 0 (52 assertions). git status: changes committed on feat/backend; .kiro/ remains untracked (not committed).

NOTE: docs keep the human/local Docker Postgres path (server/scripts/db.sh, `npm run db:up`) AND document the sandbox native-child harness the tests/e2e use — the Docker path is for a real Docker daemon; in this sandbox the native-child-over-unix-socket approach is what actually runs (Docker Postgres is unreachable across command namespaces, per FEAT-002 findings).

=== REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (2026-09-16-032543-review.md, NEEDS_CHANGES → addressed) ===
All 7 review issues resolved or justified. Final green pass after changes: root `npm test` = 77 passed, build + typecheck clean; server `npm test` = 53 passed (41 prior + 12 new security/scoping/concurrency tests), typecheck + build clean; `npm run e2e` = 52 assertions, exit 0.

1. Passwordless {userId} login — FIXED. POST /api/auth/session with {userId} is now gated behind devTools; in a prod-like app (devTools:false) it returns 403 and production login always creates a fresh user via {name}. Demo/test path (DEV_TOOLS=1 or NODE_ENV=test) still works so existing auth.test + e2e pass. Tests: security.test.ts 'arbitrary {userId} login is gated by devTools' (devTools allows 200; prod-like 403; prod-like still creates fresh user via {name}).

2. Global snapshot / no read scoping — FIXED. Added ServerRepository.scopedSnapshot(actorId): returns only the actor's world — actor + friend/chat counterparties, friendships where actor is owner OR friend (so the directional friend can still see the row), the actor's chats + those chats' messages/reads, and gift orders where actor is sender/receiver. GET /api/snapshot now calls scopedSnapshot(uid). The unscoped snapshot() remains for internal command reads (domain selectors inside a tx) only. LoginScreen 'existing users' list: in server mode there is no pre-login session so the snapshot was already empty pre-login (unchanged); a dev-only GET /api/dev/users directory endpoint (devTools-gated, 404 in prod) is provided for the demo directory. Frontend ApiRepository mirror tolerates the scoped snapshot (it already merged with emptyDb). Existing frontend tests inject LocalRepository so are unaffected (confirmed: 77 pass). Tests: security.test.ts 'scoped snapshot does not leak non-parties' (outsider C sees 0 chats/messages/gifts and only their own user; A sees their chat/message/gift + counterpart B) and 'a user sees a friendship where they are the friend'.

3. No CORS with credentialed fetch — FIXED. Registered @fastify/cors (added dependency) with credentials:true and an allowlisted origin from CLIENT_ORIGIN (comma-separated). Only registered when CLIENT_ORIGIN is set (cross-origin deploy); same-origin/local dev leaves it off. Tests: security.test.ts CORS block (allowlisted origin echoed with allow-credentials:true; non-allowlisted origin not echoed).

4. Session cookie not secure — FIXED. setSession now sets secure from config (COOKIE_SECURE=1/0 explicit, else NODE_ENV==='production'), and sameSite='none' when cross-origin (CLIENT_ORIGIN set) else 'lax'. Local http dev stays non-secure + lax so the cookie still rides. Tests: security.test.ts cookie block (prod-like → Secure + SameSite=None; local dev → not secure).

5. Idempotency race outside transaction — FIXED. withIdempotency now acquires a transaction-scoped Postgres advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock over an FNV-1a hash of scope + actor+key) on a dedicated gate connection, then does lookup → fn() → store → COMMIT atomically. Concurrent retries with the same key block on the lock and, once the first commits, read the stored result (changed:false) instead of re-executing. Tests: security.test.ts 'idempotency under concurrent retries' (4 simultaneous message retries → exactly 1 message + 1 messageId; 3 simultaneous gift retries → exactly 1 order + 1 gift message).

6. Ghost temp chat id in ApiRepository — FIXED. openDirectChat now keeps the optimistic temp chat id STABLE in the mirror (never rewrites chat.id), so a caller (App.openChat state / ChatRoomScreen) that captured it always points at a live room. The server's confirmed id is recorded in a chatIdAliases map (temp→server); outbound message/read requests translate via toServerChatId(), and incoming server snapshots are folded server→temp in replace() so the mirror stays a single stable id with no duplicate room. Updated apiRepository.test.ts openDirectChat tests to assert the ghost-free behavior (returned id still resolves after reconcile; no srv-chat-* duplicate; re-open returns the same stable id).

7. Snapshot-only reconciliation on every change signal — JUSTIFIED (documented single-instance demo scaling limit). Kept as-is; the WS fan-out carries a scope hint not a delta, so each client refetches the (now scoped) snapshot on a change. README '단일 인스턴스 인메모리 WS 팬아웃' bullet expanded to state this is sufficient at demo scale and names the future paths (per-scope delta push, Redis Pub/Sub for multi-instance fan-out). No behavior change.

Constraints honored: Repository interface (src/store/repository.ts) unchanged; gift rules still only in domain (applyGiftAction) — not reimplemented; invariants preserved (directional friendships, unique direct chats, computed unread, stored gift statuses, refund-to-payer, no-op-write emit discipline, FORCE_EXPIRE rejected at boundary, no prod reset). New env vars: CLIENT_ORIGIN, COOKIE_SECURE (documented in README.md + server/README.md).

=== REVIEW FOLLOW-UP v2 (2026-09-16-034300-review.md, NEEDS_CHANGES → addressed) ===
Pass v2 verified all 7 v1 fixes hold and found ONE new regression from the scoped-snapshot fix: the demo 'sign in as an existing user' picker ('이미 있는 사람으로 들어가기') was empty in server mode. LoginScreen builds the list from the mirror's db.users, but in server mode the mirror is empty before login (GET /api/snapshot needs a session → 401) and, after login, the scoped snapshot only carries the actor + their counterparts (never the full roster). The dev-only GET /api/dev/users directory existed on the server but (a) required a session so it could not populate pre-login, and (b) was never fetched by the frontend. So the documented two-tab demo affordance was unreachable through the UI in server mode; e2e missed it because it drives REST with cookies directly and never mounts LoginScreen.

FIX (preferred option — fold dev directory into the mirror's db.users so LoginScreen works UNCHANGED):
1. Backend (server/src/app.ts): made GET /api/dev/users session-OPTIONAL in dev mode (dropped requireUser) so the picker can populate before any login. It stays devTools-gated (404 in prod → picker simply stays empty in prod, which is correct; prod users create a fresh account via {name}). Scoped snapshot is UNTOUCHED (read-authorization fix preserved); {name} sign-up path preserved.
2. Frontend (src/store/apiRepository.ts): added ApiRepository.loadDirectory() which fetches GET /api/dev/users (credentials:'include') and folds the returned users into the in-memory mirror's db.users via the existing mutate() (upsert by id, emit-on-change discipline honored). Called once in the constructor alongside hydrate(). Because LoginScreen reads db.users, the picker now populates in server mode with NO change to LoginScreen and NO change to the SYNCHRONOUS Repository interface (loadDirectory is an out-of-interface method, like signInExisting/currentUser/signOutSession). In prod the 404 is swallowed silently → empty picker. Post-login the scoped snapshot replaces the mirror, but LoginScreen is no longer shown (App renders it only when !me), so the fold is only needed pre-login where the snapshot is 401 and does not overwrite it.

TESTS proving the picker populates in server mode:
- Frontend src/store/apiRepository.test.ts: FakeBackend gained a devTools flag + /api/dev/users route + requireSessionForSnapshot (401 pre-login). New tests: '로그인 전(세션 없음)에도 /api/dev/users 로 로그인 목록을 채운다' (snapshot 401, yet mirror.db.users = [홍길동, 김철수]) and '운영(devTools off)에서는 /api/dev/users 가 404 라 목록이 비어 있다' (empty picker in prod). Frontend suite 77 → 79.
- Backend server/test/security.test.ts: new 'dev user directory populates the demo login list without a session (pre-login)' — GET /api/dev/users with NO cookie returns 200 + both users, while GET /api/snapshot with no cookie returns 401 (the contrast that motivates the directory). Backend suite 53 → 54.

FINAL GREEN PASS v2: root npm test = 79 passed, npm run build ok, npm run typecheck ok. server npm test = 54 passed (real Postgres via vitest globalSetup), npm run typecheck ok, npm run build ok, npm run e2e = 52 assertions exit 0. git status: committed on feat/backend; .kiro/ untracked (not committed). Invariants and all v1/v2 fixes preserved: scoped snapshot unchanged, gated login (403 in prod), CORS allowlist+credentials, secure cookie, atomic advisory-lock idempotency, stable chat id; full roster NOT exposed in production (404); {name} sign-up path works.
